Subject: Request: compute stipend (trial credits) — accounting treatment & offset approach

Hi team,

Quick ask — TrialCorp (Eva Moreno) asked for a 90-day extension and a $12,000 compute stipend (promo credits) to keep them in the platform while they finish an integration. Sales signed off; procurement asked for formal accounting language for how the credit will appear on their invoices.

Questions for Finance/Billing:
- Is this posted as a formal credit memo (negative invoice) applying to the open invoice, or should we record a proforma promotional allowance and apply as an invoice offset when the next invoice issues?
- What GLA should we use for the credit (marketing/promo expense vs. contra-revenue)? Need exact GL string for our accountant (and audit).
- From an accrual standpoint, do we need to recognize any revenue reversal now or treat as contra-revenue when the credit is applied?

Attachments: Credit_Approval_Form_3981.pdf (signed by customer), Draft_Credit_Memo_3981.docx (sales ops template).

Can you advise by EOD tomorrow? Customer is waiting on procurement language.

Folks — thanks, this is helpful. High level guidance below; Marcus will confirm mechanics.

1) Recommendation: issue a formal credit memo tied to the customer account (not cash refund). Rationale: preserves traceability for audits and cleanly reduces receivables if there are outstanding invoices. If customer currently has no balance, it will sit as a customer credit to be applied against future invoices.

2) GLA mapping: use contra-revenue code (we code promotional credits as contra-revenue rather than marketing expense). Please use GLA: 4005-PROMO-CONTRA. This aligns with our revenue reporting and prevents misstating marketing spend.

3) Revenue recognition / accrual: No reversal needed on already-recognized revenue for prior closed periods unless there was revenue recognized incorrectly for the period in which the credit applies. Treat as a contra-revenue adjustment at time of application. If the credit is retroactive to a closed month and material (> $5k), flag for controller review.

4) Documentation: include signed Credit_Approval_Form_3981.pdf and a DocuSign entry or an ERP memo. For audit, retain the signed approval and the draft credit memo.

Marcus — can you confirm process to generate credit memo ID and whether we should route this as a manual credit vs. system-issued hold?

-Neha
Director, Finance Ops

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: compute stipend (trial credits) — accounting treatment & offset approach

Confirmed with billing ops:
- We'll create a system credit memo (CM-3981) in the billing system and tag with GLA 4005-PROMO-CONTRA. That will generate a negative line item on the account.
- If the customer has an outstanding invoice, we can apply CM-3981 directly to that invoice. If not, it will show as an unapplied credit on the customer balance and automatically offset the next invoice.
- For ERP posting, we'll post a journal entry debiting Sales Discounts (4005) and crediting Accounts Receivable (1200-AR) when we apply the credit.

Process steps I will do today:
1) Generate CM-3981 in the billing console.
2) Attach signed approval and the draft memo to the system credit.
3) Notify customer ops to apply the credit or leave unapplied per customer preference.

Lauren — looped to confirm whether legal needs to sign the credit memo language.

Thanks,
